data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains rather than describes when it is a guard that never fires on its author: the 3-of-26 result is the residue of a test suite designed to fail loudly for others but remain silent for the author's own installed path, so the distribution is a signature of authorial blind spots, not subject structure.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a mutation authored by someone else and planted in the same location is also missed, then the blindness is not author-specific.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the author's own edits to guarded modules are caught at a higher rate than the 3/26 baseline, then the guard does fire on its author.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distribution is stable across different authors' mutation sets, then it is structural, not biographical.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the compile.py loss was caught in a later audit without ritual change, then the weakness was transient, not authorial.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The record's insight \u2014 'a process guard that never fires on its author is probably not a guard' \u2014 suggests the test suite is an enforcement mechanism tuned to catch violations in unfamiliar code, not to describe the code it was written alongside. The shown-to-fail-first installation ritual encodes the author's own failure expectations, so mutations that preserve the author's intended semantics are invisible. The 1/9 compile.py loss is a guard that fired on the author's own edit but was silently weakened; the 3/26 spread is the set of mutations that fell within the author's unexamined assumptions.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
